analysis: Examined head-side excerpts of landing/package-lock.json (lines 796-2367). The patch bumps the landing site's Next.js from 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 and the sharp/libvips optional native packages from 0.34.5/1.2.4 to 0.35.5/1.3.4. Related @next/* and swc entries are updated. The visible head entries all use resolved URLs on registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity hashes, and I saw no git, file or http URL substitutions and no integrity fields dropped. Optional platform-specific packages are intact. The new sharp engines field requires Node >=20.9.0, a build-compatibility note, not a security issue. One win32-ia32 entry shows a Node range of ^20.9.0 only; this looks like an upstream quirk. The dev-only entries (tailwind, typescript-eslint, etc.) are unchanged in the visible range. This is a frontend marketing-site dependency lockfile change. It does not touch the provider/coordinator WebSocket contract, the attestation chain, key custody, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the cache or the fan helper, so the threat-model assets (A-001..A-018) and boundaries are unaffected. No new attack surface is evident. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the file is only partially visible (lines 796-2367 of roughly 4000). I did not verify the integrity hashes against the registry, and I did not evaluate the new packages for upstream vulnerabilities. Lockfile integrity is only as trustworthy as the registry, which is a supply-chain assumption outside the retained threat model. No regressions identified.
